iconography: Warrior on a bed of arrows

biography.early_life: Born as Devavrata, Bhishma was trained in statecraft, warfare, and Vedic wisdom. He was renowned for his intellect, discipline, and martial prowess.
biography.final_days: Felled by Arjuna with Shikhandi’s help, Bhishma lay on a bed of arrows, imparting teachings on dharma, kingship, and ethics to Yudhishthira before choosing the time of his death.
biography.legacy: Bhishma is remembered as the embodiment of steadfast duty, sacrifice, and moral complexity. His life and teachings continue to inspire ideals of leadership, selflessness, and devotion to truth.
biography.role_in_mahabharata: Bhishma served as the guardian and mentor of the Kuru princes, upholding dharma and guiding the kingdom through turbulent times. He led the Kaurava army in the Kurukshetra war and was revered for his wisdom and sense of duty.
biography.the_terrible_vow: To fulfill his father’s wish, Bhishma took a lifelong vow of celibacy and renounced his claim to the throne, earning the name 'Bhishma' for this awesome sacrifice.

timeline.event: Born as Devavrata to Shantanu and Ganga; trained in statecraft and warfare
Takes vow of celibacy and renounces claim to the throne; receives Iccha-Mrityu boon
Abduction at swayamvara; Amba’s grievance and vow foreshadow Bhishma’s fall via Shikhandi
Mentors Pandavas and Kauravas; serves as stabilizing force in Hastinapura
Leads Kaurava army; advises avoidance of battle with Shikhandi
Felled by Arjuna using Shikhandi’s presence; remains alive by will
In Shanti and Anushasana Parvas, instructs Yudhishthira on Dharma, kingship, charity, and ethics
Chooses time of death during Uttarayana; attains peace in Krishna’s presence
